title: Lowpoly Arbitrary N-Gon Faces And Coplanar Merge
description: Support arbitrary vertex/edge count faces (n-gons) in the lowpoly mesh kernel end to end: Newell-method face normals (robust for non-planar/collinear-first-corner n-gons), ear-clipping triangulation replacing the convex-only fan (tessellate, triangulate command, UV unwrap), and a real merge_coplanar_faces + dissolve_edges implementation (currently a no-op stub) with a collinear-vertex cleanup pass. Regenerate the "Concrete Forest Left" default example mesh with all coplanar faces merged into n-gons instead of the current all-triangle tessellated output.
summary:
Implemented arbitrary n-gon face support in the halfedge mesh kernel and regenerated the default "Concrete Forest Left" example with coplanar faces merged, then fixed a watertightness bug in the regenerated mesh reported after initial delivery.

Kernel (kernel/3d/mesh/rs/lib.rs):
- Rewrote face_normal to use Newell's method (robust for concave/non-planar loops) instead of a first-triangle cross product.
- Added a private ear-clipping triangulator (f64 plane-projection + deterministic ear clipping with fan fallback) and wired it into tessellate(), triangulate(), and solve_island_uv(), replacing naive corner-0 fans.
- Implemented merge_coplanar_faces() (greedy adjacent-face merge by Newell-normal parallelism + planarity tolerance) and a collinear_cleanup pass that drops redundant ~180° pass-through vertices.
- Implemented dissolve_edges() for real (was a no-op stub), sharing the pairwise face-merge core with merge_coplanar_faces.
- Added weld_coincident_vertices(precision) to unify accidentally duplicated coincident vertices (compacts the position array, not just a remap).
- Added fill_holes() using proper halfedge-rotation boundary tracing (walks next/twin around a boundary half-edge's destination vertex to find the correctly paired next boundary edge of the SAME hole) — this correctly disambiguates multiple separate holes sharing one corner vertex, which a naive vertex-to-vertex "next" map cannot do.
- Fixed two broken test attributes (a doubled #[test], and triangulate_produces_triangles_only which was never running).
- Added 9 new permanent unit tests covering Newell normals, ear clipping, coplanar merge, edge dissolve, collinear cleanup, tessellation of concave faces, vertex welding, and hole filling (incl. the two-holes-sharing-a-vertex case). All temporary diagnostic tests used during root-cause investigation were removed after the fix was confirmed.

Example regeneration (lowpoly/core/rs/tests/export_concrete_forest_mesh.rs):
- Pipeline is now: from_indexed_triangles → weld_coincident_vertices(1e-4) → fill_holes() → merge_coplanar_faces() → assert_watertight() → center/unwrap_uv → export. Order matters: weld first for accurate topology, fill_holes before merge so new cap faces can also participate in coplanar merging.
- Added assert_watertight() (directed-edge reciprocity check) as a permanent regression test.
- Regenerated lowpoly/example/concrete-forest-left.mesh.json and lowpoly/example/default.lowpoly.json via the ticket-folder script export-concrete-forest-mesh.ts. Final stats: 70 vertices, 372 halfedges, 77 faces (mix of quads/triangles/hexagons/octagons/heptagons/pentagons and two large n-gons), 0 open boundary edges.

Root cause of the watertightness bug: the mesh was never geometrically broken — the original fill_holes implementation used a vertex-to-vertex "next along boundary" HashMap, which silently overwrote entries when a vertex had more than one outgoing boundary edge (37+ vertices did, from multiple separate holes sharing corner vertices). Replacing it with true halfedge-rotation boundary tracing fixed it; weld_coincident_vertices found 0 duplicates on the real asset, confirming duplicate vertices were never the issue.

Verified: cargo test -p kernel_3d_mesh (22 passing) and cargo test -p lowpoly_core (13 + 3 passing, including the new watertightness assertion) both green. Rebuilt the lowpoly plugin wasm and visually confirmed in the browser (lowpoly-react-dev, port 6078): the regenerated mesh loads with the expected 70/195/77 vertex/edge/face counts, renders as a single solid shape with no visible gaps, and no console errors.
